about: The smallest play area (CSS px: the space Vault’s player gives a game below its bar) each game is playable in, measured 2026-10-03 on vaultlearninggames-staging.org with Playwright/Chromium. Seeded into the listings (Smallest play area); the listings, not this file, are what the site uses. null: not measurable, the site default (hugo.toml params.play) applies.
how: Each game was opened in Vault’s player and the window was shrunk step by step, width at a 1000 px tall window (1600 down to 375) and height at a 1600 px wide one (1000 down to 320), plus 1024x768, 768x1024, 1280x720, 1366x768, 844x390, 390x844, 820x1180 and 1180x820. Games that size themselves only when they load were measured again with a fresh load at each size.
Broken: the game’s content runs out of its frame (scrollbars or a cut-off canvas inside the player), or the game shows its own rotate / too-small message.

Too small: a game that scales itself is drawn at less than 2/3 of its intended size (a Player fit’s rectangle; a fixed drawing resolution up to 1366 px wide; PhET’s 1024 x 618 layout; otherwise its size on a 1366 x 768 laptop). At 2/3, text that is 14-16 px at full size is 9.5-10.5 px, the smallest that stays readable on a school screen. Visible page text below 10 px counts too.

The minimum is the smallest step above which nothing broke, interpolated for scaling games, rounded up to 10 px; widths and heights are measured separately. Where the automatic rules misread a game, the value was judged from the screenshots (method: judged).
